# Compatibility Checklist: Every Edge of the Graph Gets an Id

**Purpose**: Test whether the requirements of #285 say clearly what changes for those who read the graph export — files of format 1.0, the published JSON schema, Maxitor and the other readers in this repository.
**Created**: 2026-10-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the readers of the export in this repository listed as a closed list, so FR-012 can be checked against each one — including the demo endpoint that serves the export (`get_example_model_graph_json_action`) and Maxitor's own-model resource? [Completeness, Spec §Context, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec say what changes for a reader in each of the four ways the export changes — a new field, a new edge order, a new version string, a stricter schema? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, §FR-011]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK003 Is "the same diagram" in SC-005 defined — the same elements only, or also the same layout and row order — given that the order of edges in the export changes (FR-010)? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-005, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 Is "keep working unchanged" in FR-012 tied to a named check for each reader, rather than left as a general promise? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK005 Does the spec acknowledge that the order by id is not the `(source_id, type, target_id)` order it replaces — `|` sorts after `.`, so `a.b.c|…` comes before `a.b|…` — and say whether any reader relied on the old order? [Consistency, Spec §Context, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK006 Do the spec and the contract agree on what the public function does with a row that already carries an `id` — the contract ignores it, the spec says nothing (trust it? refuse a mismatch?)? [Conflict, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007, contracts/edge-identity.md]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the error a reader of a 1.0 file must expect named the same way everywhere — the spec says "an error naming the type and the property", the data model says `ValueError` for a reader and `InvalidGraphError` at build? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, §FR-009, data-model.md §Refusals]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK008 Is the reader's behaviour defined when two rows of a 1.0 file compute the same id — a file written before the build refused duplicates (FR-008)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the reader's behaviour defined for a file whose `schema_version` is neither `"1.0"` nor `"1.1"`? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK010 Is the assumption that every 1.0 file carries `field_name` on `entity_relation` and `from_state` on `lifecycle_transition` checked against the oldest files the history will read (gameoffer's snapshots 001–006), not only 005 and 006? [Assumption, Spec §FR-007, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK011 Is it stated that a 1.0 file no longer validates against the published schema, and that this is intended? [Assumption, Spec §FR-011, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the promise to readers outside this repository explicit — gameoffer's snapshots and CI, services that validate their own export — and does the documentation (FR-013) tell them what to do? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-012, §FR-013]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
